title: Same as Ever
author: Morgan Housel
blurb: Morgan Housel argues that we waste energy trying to forecast events no one can foresee, when the smarter move is to understand the things about people that stay constant across history. Through short, story-driven chapters, he shows how greed, fear, and the stories we tell ourselves repeat in every era. The biggest risks are the ones nobody sees coming, so preparation beats prediction. Happiness depends less on what we have and more on what we expect. A compelling story often beats the plain truth. Long periods of calm quietly encourage the risky behaviour that ends them. Bad news arrives suddenly, while good news builds slowly and goes unnoticed. The practical takeaway is to build a life and finances with room for error, accept that volatility is the price of reward, and anchor decisions to what history shows never changes.

lessons.b: Instead of predicting specific events, focus on the human behaviours that stay the same across every era.
